title: Engine Oil Filter Housing Drain Nozzle and Shroud Change

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Changes the oil filter housing drain nozzle and its shroud so that the housing can be drained without spillage onto the pylon fairing, after oil staining below the engine became a recurring cosmetic and inspection nuisance.

sections.reason: Oil staining on the pylon lower fairing was reported by nine operators and always cleaned as a cosmetic item, but it also masked the leak checks that follow any engine work and had twice led to an unnecessary component change. The drain nozzle as delivered discharges into a shroud with an open lower edge, and residual oil in the housing runs down the shroud rather than into the collection point during a filter change.
sections.description: The drain nozzle is replaced by a variant with a bayonet fitting for the drain hose, so that the housing can be drained directly to a container, and the shroud is replaced by a closed profile with a lip that routes any residual oil to the same fitting. The washer at the housing joint is changed to the current standard. The filter element, the housing and the oil pump are unchanged. The installation drawing is reissued for the new shroud profile and the hose attachment point.
sections.effects: Mass increase of zero point five kilograms per engine. No electrical load change. Interchangeable at aircraft level; the nozzle and shroud must be changed as a pair. The drain task changes substantially because the hose is now attached before the housing is opened, saving about twenty minutes and removing the spillage clean-up. The oil pressure troubleshooting entry is reissued because it calls out the drain step.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in at MSN M00377. Retrofit by bulletin at any filter change; a second bulletin at revision two extends the effectivity to the larger variant and corrects the hose part call-out.

type_data.production_impact: Cut in at MSN M00377, vendor supplies the closed shroud
